clue.text: Referee's aid wrong to overturn Honda's opener for Japan?

indicators.note: overturning a word in an across clue turns its letters back to front
the opener of a name is its first letter, so only the start of 'Honda' is used

blocks.note: VAR, the video assistant referee used in football
a wrong is a sin; overturned it becomes NIS
first letter of the carmaker's name

explanation.surface: A car maker's crash is being checked on a video replay, with Japan as the team concerned.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Japan' looks like the country after 'Honda', but lower-case japan is a hard black lacquer; the question mark flags it as an example of the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Japan is a glossy black lacquer originally from that country, so it is one kind of shiny protective coating.

clue.text: Very deep bottles start to tempt one into wine

indicators.note: to bottle something is to hold it inside, so the word for deep holds the start of tempt
the start of a word is its first letter, so only the opening of 'tempt' is taken

blocks.note: V is the standard abbreviation for very
deep in the sense of lying far inside
the first letter, placed inside the word for deep

explanation.surface: A sommelier warns that a very rich wine in its bottles can lure one into drinking too much.
explanation.walkthrough: 'One into wine' is a jokey phrase for someone whose trade is wine, not someone keen on drinking it; VINTNER is the wine merchant.
explanation.definitionFit: A vintner deals in or makes wine for a living, so wine is literally their business and line of work.

clue.text: Rocks fish is found under, right?

indicators.note: in a down clue, one piece found under another is written below it, so the fish follows the abbreviation

blocks.note: R is the usual abbreviation for right
fish is = fish's, the eel's, read as EELS

explanation.surface: A rock-pooler asks whether the fish really hides under the stones.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'found under' puts the fish below the abbreviation for right. 'Rocks' is a verb here: to sway or stagger.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who staggers or sways unsteadily on their feet, as if dizzy, can be said to be lurching this way.

clue.text: Example of an insect on the rocks

indicators.note: something on the rocks is wrecked and broken up, so the letters of 'an insect' are smashed and rebuilt

blocks.note: anagram fodder, eight letters

explanation.surface: A bug perched on a stone, or floating in a drink served over ice.
explanation.walkthrough: 'On the rocks' pulls toward ice in a glass or a shipwreck; here it only means the letters are broken up.
explanation.definitionFit: An instance is a single case cited to illustrate something, which is exactly what an example does.

clue.text: Transport goods in adverse weather, imports primarily going to university

indicators.note: primarily means in first place, so only the opening letter of 'imports' counts
one letter going to another means it is swapped out for the university abbreviation

blocks.note: hail is a kind of adverse weather
first letter of imports, the letter replaced
U is the standard abbreviation for university

explanation.surface: A lorry driver moving imports through bad weather, bound for a university delivery.
explanation.walkthrough: HAIL changes its I for U. 'Transport goods' is the definition as a verb phrase: to haul freight.
explanation.definitionFit: To haul is to carry or drag a heavy load, as trucking firms do with freight over long distances.

clue.text: Frame leader of cabal while relative smuggles heroin

indicators.note: the leader of a word is its first letter, so only the start of 'cabal' is used
to smuggle is to carry something hidden inside, so the drug is tucked into the other pieces

blocks.note: first letter of cabal
as = while, meaning during the time that
sis, short for sister
H is slang for heroin

explanation.surface: A crime story: the head of a gang is set up while a family member runs drugs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Frame' looks like a verb about fitting someone up; it is a noun, the structural frame of a car. The H slips in just after the C.
explanation.definitionFit: A chassis is the base structure of a vehicle onto which body and engine are mounted, its supporting skeleton.

clue.text: Lacking time, reconstruct carelessly?

indicators.note: lacking something means going without it, so the time abbreviation is dropped from the fodder
done carelessly the letters of 'reconstruct' end up in a jumbled order

blocks.note: T is the standard abbreviation for time
anagram fodder once one T is removed

explanation.surface: A builder short of time rushes through a rebuild.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is both the wordplay and the definition: remove one T from RECONSTRUCT and rearrange, and the clue also describes skimping when short of time.
explanation.definitionFit: To take shortcuts and skimp on proper procedure, usually to save time, is the idiom's meaning.

clue.text: More playful shot

blocks.note: comparative of arch, meaning mischievous or knowing
a shot is someone who shoots, as in 'a good shot'

explanation.walkthrough: 'Shot' looks like a noun for a drink or a photo; it is a person who shoots, and a bowman is one.
explanation.definitionFit: Arch means mischievously teasing, giving a comparative form; a bowman shooting arrows is a marksman.

clue.text: Stone coming down and breaking your back

blocks.note: st is the abbreviation for stone, the British weight
rain coming down, as in 'it's coming down'

explanation.surface: A falling rock lands on someone and injures their spine.
explanation.walkthrough: ST is a stone, a British unit of weight of 14 pounds. 'Breaking your back' is the idiom for working very hard, not an injury.
explanation.definitionFit: Breaking your back is an idiom for making an enormous effort, pushing yourself to the limit of exertion.

clue.text: Directed to take in boxer striking

indicators.note: taking something in means holding it inside, so the word for directed wraps the boxer

blocks.note: sent = directed, as in sent somewhere
Muhammad Ali, the crossword's favourite boxer

explanation.surface: A boxer is told to take a punch, or directed to watch a bout.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Striking' is placed to sound like punching after 'boxer', but it is an adjective meaning prominent.
explanation.definitionFit: Salient means most noticeable or prominent, which is what something eye-catching and remarkable is.

clue.text: Ground nest emu covers in sand - there's no other choice

indicators.note: something ground is crushed up, so the letters are pulverised and rearranged
the covers of a word are its outside letters, so only the two ends of 'sand' are kept

blocks.note: anagram fodder, seven letters
first and last letters of sand

explanation.surface: An emu's nest on the ground gets buried in sand, and it can do nothing about it.
explanation.walkthrough: The saying is short for 'needs must when the devil drives'.
explanation.definitionFit: The proverb means that necessity compels you to do something unwanted, leaving you without an alternative.

clue.text: Combustible material around radiator's beginning to become orangey-pink

indicators.note: around means on all sides of, so the fuel wraps the radiator's first letter
the beginning of a word is its first letter, so only the opening of 'radiator' is used

blocks.note: coal is a fuel that burns
first letter of radiator

explanation.surface: Fuel stacked near a heater glows as it starts to warm up.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests a glowing fire; the answer is the colour of that glow.
explanation.definitionFit: Coral names a shade like that of pink and orange reef coral, a warm salmon hue.

clue.text: Rocket scientists run around cape for sport

indicators.note: around means on all sides of, so the space agency and the run surround the cape

blocks.note: NASA, the US space agency
R is the cricket scoring abbreviation for run
C is the map abbreviation for cape

explanation.surface: Engineers go jogging around Cape Canaveral for exercise.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface puts NASA beside a cape, as at Cape Canaveral, which hides how the pieces fit. NASCAR is American stock-car racing.
explanation.definitionFit: NASCAR is the American stock-car racing series, a motor sport watched by millions of fans.

clue.text: Violet bruise, extremely kinky?

indicators.note: extremely means at the extremes, so only the two end letters of 'bruise' are kept
something kinky is twisted, so the letters are bent into a new order

blocks.note: anagram fodder, six letters
first and last letters of bruise

explanation.surface: A purple mark on the skin that hints at something rather racy.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is the definition as well as the wordplay: a purple bruise left by a lover.
explanation.definitionFit: A hickey is the purplish mark left on the skin by kissing or sucking hard, often during passion.

clue.text: At the end, on top of hill, boarding fell

indicators.note: someone boarding goes inside a vehicle, so the hill gets into the word for fell

blocks.note: fell as an adjective means fierce or cruel
a tor is a rocky hill, as on Dartmoor

explanation.surface: A walker reaches the summit of a hill, then climbs a fell as well.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fell' reads as a northern English hill beside 'hill'; here it is the old adjective meaning savage, as in 'one fell swoop'.
explanation.definitionFit: Being on top when everything is over means you have won, having triumphed at the final reckoning.

clue.text: Decreases in wine sales wiping out bodega in the end

indicators.note: wiping something out removes it, so a letter is taken away from the sales
the end of a word is its last letter, so only the close of 'bodega' is meant

blocks.note: red wine
auctions are sales
last letter of bodega, removed from the sales

explanation.surface: A wine shop's sales are falling, and the business may close.
explanation.walkthrough: A bodega is a Spanish wine shop, which ties the surface together; only its last letter is used.
explanation.definitionFit: Reductions are cuts or drops in amount, which is what a list of lowered figures shows.

clue.text: Canine companion to deliberately avoid being cuddled by father

indicators.note: being cuddled means held in someone's arms, so the word for father wraps the other pieces

blocks.note: dad = father
CH, Companion of Honour, a British order
to shun is to avoid on purpose

explanation.surface: A pet dog stays away from its owner's hugs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Canine companion' looks like one phrase for the definition, but 'companion' is CH, the Companion of Honour, a British honour.
explanation.definitionFit: The sausage-shaped German breed with short legs is a dog, which is a member of the canine family.

clue.text: Cloud over coliseum is troubling crowds

indicators.note: a phrase that crowds something packs it within, so the letters sit inside the words that follow

blocks.note: the end of coliseum, the whole of is, and the start of troubling

explanation.surface: Crowds packing an arena look troubled as the weather closes in.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cloud over' is a verb phrase here, as a mirror or window does.
explanation.definitionFit: When glass mists it becomes blurred by condensation, the same as when it clouds up and loses clarity.

clue.text: System of symbols not helping - translator ultimately let go

indicators.note: ultimately means at the last, so only the final letter of 'translator' is meant
a letter let go is released and dropped from the helping

blocks.note: used as it stands
a helping of food is a ration
last letter of translator, the one dropped

explanation.surface: A translator gets fired because their code of symbols was no help.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Not helping' reads as one phrase, but it splits: NOT as written, then helping as a noun meaning a portion.
explanation.definitionFit: Notation is a set of written signs used to represent things, such as musical or mathematical characters.

clue.text: Crowd pleaser right not to get involved in outrageous comedy

indicators.note: right that will not be involved is kept out, so that letter is removed from the comedy

blocks.note: R is the usual abbreviation for right
a farce is an outrageous, far-fetched comedy

explanation.surface: A comedian who wants to please the audience decides to steer clear of slapstick.
explanation.walkthrough: In professional wrestling a face (short for babyface) is the hero the crowd cheers, opposite the heel.
explanation.definitionFit: In wrestling slang the good-guy performer whom fans cheer is called this, as opposed to the villainous heel.

clue.text: Hairdresser to stand up cutting hair

indicators.note: something cutting into another goes inside it, so the word for stand up sits within the word for hair

blocks.note: an animal's fur is its hair
to rise is to stand up

explanation.surface: A barber tells a customer to stand while having their hair cut.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cutting hair' sounds like the hairdresser's job, but cutting only says one piece goes inside the other.
explanation.definitionFit: Friseur is a French and German loanword for a barber or stylist, someone who styles people's locks.

clue.text: Astrologer working with government welcomed by PM

indicators.note: someone welcomed by a host is taken in, so the prime minister wraps the other pieces

blocks.note: Keir Starmer, UK Prime Minister
on = working, as a machine that is switched on
G is an abbreviation for government

explanation.surface: A political news item: a stargazer joins a government team and is greeted by the prime minister.
explanation.walkthrough: Keir Starmer became UK Prime Minister in 2024. A starmonger is an old, dismissive word for an astrologer.
explanation.definitionFit: A starmonger is a scornful term for someone who peddles horoscopes and predictions read from the heavens.

clue.text: I admire that muscle clenched by others

indicators.note: something clenched is gripped tightly, so the word for others holds the muscle

blocks.note: the rest = the others
pec, short for pectoral muscle

explanation.surface: An admirer compliments someone on the chest muscles they are flexing.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is an exclamation, the slang 'Respect!' said in admiration.
explanation.definitionFit: Said on its own as an interjection, the word expresses approval and esteem for someone's achievement.

clue.text: Bitter ale in cellar initially probed by detectives

indicators.note: initially means at the start, so each of 'ale in cellar' gives its first letter
to probe is to push into something, so the detectives go inside the initials

blocks.note: first letters of the three words
CID, the Criminal Investigation Department of British police

explanation.surface: Police raid a pub cellar and find the beer has gone sour.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bitter ale' looks like the British beer style, but 'Bitter' alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Something acidic tastes sharp and sour, which is close in sense to a harsh or tart flavour.

clue.text: Hot and dry river lacking locks?

blocks.note: hot = in, fashionable
sec, the French wine term for dry
the Ure, a Yorkshire river

explanation.surface: A hot, parched riverbed with no locks on the waterway.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Locks' seems to be canal locks on a river; the question mark flags it as door locks. The Ure is a river in Yorkshire, England.
explanation.definitionFit: A building with no bolts or fastenings is unprotected, so the word for unsafe fits it literally.

clue.text: Grounds for educating about politician in Australia

indicators.note: one thing in another sits inside it, so the politician goes within the abbreviation for Australia

blocks.note: c = circa, about
AUS, the abbreviation for Australia
MP, Member of Parliament

explanation.surface: A politician is lecturing about education policy on a visit to Australia.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Grounds' looks like reasons; it is the land a college stands on.
explanation.definitionFit: A campus is the site and buildings of a university or college, where students are taught.

clue.text: Parking on raised road constituting a fine

indicators.note: in a down clue, raising a word makes it read from bottom to top

blocks.note: P is the road-sign abbreviation for parking
a lane is a road

explanation.surface: A parking ticket issued on an elevated road.
explanation.walkthrough: 'On' puts the P on top of the rest in a down clue. 'A fine' is the thing a penalty takes the form of.
explanation.definitionFit: Penal describes something serving as punishment, and a monetary penalty is exactly such a sanction.

clue.text: Shorter exercise needing no working

indicators.note: needing no means doing without, so the word for working is removed from the exercise

blocks.note: a lesson is a piece of schoolwork, an exercise
on = working, switched on

explanation.surface: A teacher sets a shorter task that needs no workings shown.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Working' looks like the maths workings in the surface; it is ON, as a machine is on.
explanation.definitionFit: Less means smaller in amount or extent, which a briefer or reduced thing is.

clue.text: Term for twenty-five pounds is pony?

definitions.text: Term for twenty-five pounds is pony?

blocks.clueFragment: Term for twenty-five pounds is pony
blocks.note: surface reading: in British slang a pony is twenty-five pounds sterling
setter's reading: a pony is a small horse, so the term needed is the zoological family word that covers it

explanation.walkthrough: The money slang is the decoy, and the answer looks like 'e' plus quid, British slang for a pound, which fits the pounds theme.
explanation.definitionFit: Horses, donkeys, zebras and ponies all belong to the horse family, whose members are called by this zoological name.

clue.text: Submissiveness in bed liked regularly when edging

indicators.note: regularly means at even intervals, so every other letter of 'liked' is taken
edging something means forming its border, so the word for when goes around the other pieces

blocks.note: once = when, as in 'once it starts'
used as it stands
second and fourth letters of liked

explanation.surface: A racy scene: submission in the bedroom, enjoyed now and then, while holding back.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface is deliberately risqué; each word does a plain job in the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: Obedience is compliance with orders, the quality of yielding to someone else's authority.

clue.text: Censors bloody shows

blocks.note: blood is red
acts are shows, or turns in one

explanation.surface: A film censor cuts violent programmes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Censors' looks like the people who cut; it is the verb, and 'bloody' is the colour of blood rather than an expletive.
explanation.definitionFit: To redact a document is to black out sensitive passages before it is released, a form of editing out.

clue.text: Wrestling gear itches with skirt the wrong way round

indicators.note: a word's skirt is its outer edge, so the two end letters of the word for itches trade places

blocks.note: tingles = itches, prickly sensations

explanation.surface: A wrestler's kit is uncomfortable, with a skirt put on back to front.
explanation.walkthrough: Only the outer letters of TINGLES trade places; the middle INGLE stays as it is. A singlet is the one-piece suit amateur wrestlers wear.
explanation.definitionFit: Amateur wrestlers compete in a tight one-piece sleeveless suit, which is the standard uniform of the sport.
